615:
616:def run_public_search(
617:    config: PublicRunConfig,
618:    contract: PuzzleContract,
619:    model: ExportedModel,
620:    plan: RuntimePlan,
621:    weights_dir: Path,
622:    artifact_dir: Path,
623:    *,
624:    runner_path: str = "production_runner",
625:) -> RunArtifacts:
626:    """Run requested variants and retain only CPU-validated original-oriented paths."""
627:    del model
628:    external_sources = _reflection_sources(config, contract)  # Must finish before any GPU launch.
629:    if config.solution_mode == "collect":
630:        derive_solved_result_capacity(plan, contract.move_count)
631:    submission = contract.sample_submission.copy(deep=True)
632:    submission_column = _submission_column(submission)
633:    records: list[SolutionRecord] = []
634:    executions: list[InvocationExecution] = []
635:    statuses: list[CollectionStatus] = []
636:
637:    def execute(invocation: RunnerInvocation) -> ParsedRunnerOutput:
638:        try:
639:            execution = _run_one(invocation, {})
640:        except InvocationLogCaptureError as error:
641:            execution = error.execution
642:            executions.append(execution)
643:            partial = _build_artifacts(records, submission, executions, statuses)
644:            raise PublicSearchRunError(
645:                f"production runner failed for puzzle {invocation.puzzle_id} {invocation.variant} "
646:                f"with exit code {execution.return_code}; runner postprocess failed: {error}",
647:                partial,
648:            ) from error
649:        executions.append(execution)
650:        if execution.return_code != 0:
651:            partial = _build_artifacts(records, submission, executions, statuses)
652:            raise PublicSearchRunError(
653:                f"production runner failed for puzzle {invocation.puzzle_id} {invocation.variant} "
654:                f"with exit code {execution.return_code}",
655:                partial,
656:            )
657:        parsed = parse_runner_output(
658:            execution.output, invocation.result_tsv, invocation.puzzle_id, invocation.variant
659:        )
660:        statuses.append(parsed.collection_status)
661:        return parsed
662:
663:    for puzzle_id in config.puzzle_ids:
664:        discovered_sources: list[tuple[str, str]] = list(external_sources[puzzle_id])
665:        if config.reflect_mode != "only":
666:            invocation = build_runner_invocation(
667:                config, plan, contract.move_count, puzzle_id, "original", weights_dir, artifact_dir,
668:                runner_path=runner_path,
669:            )
670:            original_records = _validated_records(execute(invocation), contract, puzzle_id, "original")
671:            records.extend(original_records)
672:            if config.reflect_mode == "after_original":
673:                discovered_sources.extend(
674:                    (record.original_oriented_path, sha256(record.original_oriented_path.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest())
675:                    for record in original_records
676:                )
677:        if config.reflect_mode in {"after_original", "only"}:
678:            sources = sorted(set(discovered_sources), key=lambda item: (_path_depth(item[0]), item[0], item[1]))
679:            for source_path, source_sha256 in sources:
680:                reflected_state = make_reflected_state(contract.central_state, source_path, contract.generators)
681:                invocation = build_runner_invocation(
682:                    config, plan, contract.move_count, puzzle_id, "reflected", weights_dir, artifact_dir,
683:                    runner_path=runner_path, source_solution_sha256=source_sha256,
684:                )
685:                _write_reflected_test_row(invocation, puzzle_id, reflected_state)
686:                records.extend(_validated_records(
687:                    execute(invocation), contract, puzzle_id, "reflected",
688:                    reflected_state=reflected_state, source_sha256=source_sha256,
689:                ))
690:
691:        records = deduplicate_solutions(records)
692:        puzzle_records = [record for record in records if record.puzzle_id == puzzle_id]
693:        if puzzle_records:
694:            best = min(
695:                puzzle_records,
696:                key=lambda record: (
697:                    _path_depth(record.original_oriented_path),
698:                    record.original_oriented_path,
699:                    0 if record.variant == "original" else 1,
700:                    record.source_solution_sha256 or "",
701:                ),
702:            )
703:            submission.loc[
704:                submission["initial_state_id"] == puzzle_id, submission_column
705:            ] = best.original_oriented_path
706:
707:    return _build_artifacts(records, submission, executions, statuses)

- **P0 — First-solution mode cannot parse the normal production build.** `parse_runner_output` accepts only `solution_path=...`, but `production_runner` emits that key only under disabled-by-default debug logging. - **P1 — Public runner environment is not hermetic.** `_run_one` inherits every process variable except three rank keys. Existing `BEAM_REPAIR_SOLUTIONS_CSV`, state/target overrides, `BEAM_RING_COUNT`, and other unowned `BEAM_*` controls survive and can silently change the public run despite the explicit manual profile. [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:468)

- **P1 — Valid reflection sources are excluded from shortest-path/submission selection.** External sources are used only to seed reflected launches; they never become validated candidate records. In `only`, no reflected hit leaves the sample placeholder unchanged, while a longer reflected result can win despite a shorter validated source. [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:664), [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:691)

- **P1 — Chunked NCCL gather still has capacity-sized host aggregation.** Device send/receive ranges and collective ordering are correct, but every chunk is accumulated into one global `records` vector and every record is reconstructed before the host capacity stop. At beam `2**21`, 24 moves permits roughly 50 million gathered records per process even when `MAX_COLLECTED_SOLUTIONS=3`, risking host OOM and defeating bounded collection. [production_runner.cu](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/production_runner.cu:3194), [production_runner.cu](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/production_runner.cu:4672)

- **P2 — Reflection inverse closure is checked after GPU work.** `invert_path` can reject a generator set without unique named inverses only after the reflected subprocess completes, contrary to reflection preflight/fail-before-launch behavior. [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:596), [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:687)

- **P2 — Exceptional cleanup can race the live rank group and mask diagnostics.** If streaming fails, `_run_one` immediately removes history scratch without terminating/waiting for torchrun. A cleanup failure then replaces the original stream/log exception before an `InvocationExecution` and partial artifacts exist. [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:475), [runner.py](D:/100XH100/.worktrees/public-cayleypy-notebook/tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py:495)

# Project Agent Rules

## Operating Rule
- Read `AGENTS.md` before project edits.
- Update `memory/CHANGELOG.md` after meaningful code, config, or architecture changes.
- Update `memory/PROMPTS.md` with user prompts that define requirements.
- Store test outputs, logs, and verification notes under `test_results/`.
- Prefer agent-centered code: explicit contracts, deterministic tests, small files, low hidden state.

## Architecture Source
- Primary architecture contract: `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md`.
- Current Stream 4 implementation rule: use threshold + compact + CUB/fixed-temp sort/reduce + compact; do not use Stream 4 hash-table dedup.

## Implementation Guardrails
- `State128` logical bytes are `v[0..119]`.
- `State128` padding bytes are `v[120..127]`.
- Persistent frontier padding must be zero.
- `FinalResponse` may temporarily store `target_local_idx` in `v[120..123]`.
- `Hash128` is one logical 128-bit key stored as `{lo, hi}`.
- `CandidateMeta` must remain 32 bytes and 32-byte aligned.
- Stream 3 payload id must be original candidate id, not compact index.
- Stream 4 must not apply shard top-k or semantic shard cap.

# HighloadGpu

Router for CUDA code-writing and high-performance GPU engineering. Default to a single-GPU CUDA hot path first; use multi-GPU or search/decoding guidance only when the task calls for it.

## Pick The Sub-Skill

- CUDA kernels, memory layout, CUTLASS/CUB, graphs, native hot paths: `write-cuda-hot-paths`
- Beam search, top-k/top-p decoding, frontier expansion, candidate selection: `optimize-gpu-search-and-decoding`
- Multi-GPU scaling, rank ownership, peer access, NCCL, overlap: `design-multigpu-systems`
- Python/Rust/C++/CUDA ownership boundaries: `choose-stack-boundaries`
- GPU model, compute capability, CUDA/library docs: `use-nvidia-docs`
- Timeline/stream/NCCL/launch gaps: `use-nsight-systems`
- One-kernel bottleneck: `use-nsight-compute`
- Illegal access/race/init/sync bug: `use-compute-sanitizer`
- Batch/concurrency/shard sweeps: `benchmark-and-sweep-gpu-configs`
- Kaggle/Molab/remote GPU profiling: `profile-remote-gpu-runs`

## Defaults

- Python: wrappers, notebooks, dashboards, CLI/torchrun launch.
- Rust: safe config, validation, artifact/log tooling, host services.
- C++ + CUDA: CPU/GPU hot paths, kernels, CUDA Graphs, NCCL, CUTLASS, CUB/CCCL.

Check current NVIDIA docs before hardware-specific advice. Require correctness checks and profiling evidence before architecture changes.

name: optimize-gpu-search-and-decoding
description: Use when optimizing beam search, top-k/top-p decoding, frontier expansion, candidate selection, or GPU search loops.
---

# Optimize GPU Search And Decoding

Specialized router for search-like GPU workloads. Keep this separate from general CUDA code-writing and from multi-GPU scaling. Load `references/search-decoding-patterns.md` when implementation details are needed.

## Scope

- Beam search, tree/graph frontier expansion, top-k/top-p decoding, candidate pruning, ranked selection, dynamic active sets, and sequence/history materialization.
- Use `write-cuda-hot-paths` for generic kernel/layout implementation details.
- Use `design-multigpu-systems` only when the search loop must cross GPU or rank boundaries.

## Design Defaults

- Split the loop into explicit phases: score, expand, filter, select, compact, materialize.
- Represent active sets with fixed-capacity arrays, offsets, masks, and counts. Add overflow paths; do not silently clamp.
- Preallocate all candidate, scratch, temp, and history buffers before the repeated loop.
- Prefer CUB/CCCL scan/select/sort/reduce and segmented operations before custom global synchronization.
- Keep histories compact with token IDs, parent pointers, offsets, or backpointers; materialize full outputs only at selected boundaries.

---
name: design-multigpu-systems
description: Use when scaling CUDA workloads across multiple GPUs, ranks, or nodes.
---

# Design Multi-GPU Systems

Use only when a workload needs multiple devices, ranks, or nodes. Keep search, beam, and decoding algorithms in `optimize-gpu-search-and-decoding`. Load `references/multigpu-patterns.md` when implementation details are needed.

## Core Rules

- Define rank/device ownership before writing kernels: inputs, outputs, scratch, streams, communicators, and host control state.
- Choose the split: data parallel, model/tensor parallel, pipeline parallel, task sharding, or replicated workers.
- Keep local GPU work local; cross-device exchange should happen at explicit boundaries.
- Preallocate device memory, CUB temp, NCCL buffers, graph resources, and host pinned buffers before steady-state loops.
- Verify NCCL ordering is identical on all ranks and log rank/device/collective sequence numbers.
- Inspect topology, exchange volume, load balance, host launch serialization, and synchronization before changing kernels.

- Create: `tools/cayleypy_public/runner.py`
- Create: `tools/run_cayleypy_public.py`

In collect mode assert `BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_MODE=1`, `BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_STOP_DEPTH=COLLECT_UNTIL_DEPTH`, and `BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_MAX_SOLUTIONS=MAX_COLLECTED_SOLUTIONS`. Assert no inherited `WORLD_SIZE/RANK/LOCAL_RANK`.

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement mode orchestration**

For `off`, run originals. For `after_original`, use every validated original source selected by mode, synthesize a temporary standard test row, run reflected search, invert, and revalidate. For `only`, validate every supplied source path before any GPU launch. In all modes, update submission with the shortest valid original-oriented path.

171:def derive_solved_result_capacity(plan: RuntimePlan, move_count: int) -> int:
172:    """Bound one rank's worst-case Stream2 hits for a completed depth."""
173:    if isinstance(move_count, bool) or not isinstance(move_count, int) or move_count <= 0:
174:        raise ValueError("move_count must be a positive integer")
175:    if plan.local_beam <= 0:
176:        raise ValueError("local_beam must be positive")
177:    capacity = plan.local_beam * move_count
178:    if capacity > _UINT32_MAX:
179:        raise ValueError("BEAM_SOLVED_RESULT_CAPACITY exceeds uint32")
180:    snapshot_bytes = capacity * _SOLVED_RECORD_BYTES
181:    frontier_bytes = plan.local_beam * 128
182:    required_bytes = snapshot_bytes + frontier_bytes
183:    available_bytes = _T4_DEVICE_BYTES - _T4_HEADROOM_BYTES
184:    if required_bytes > available_bytes:
185:        raise ValueError(
186:            "BEAM_SOLVED_RESULT_CAPACITY snapshot plus current frontier exceeds available T4 device memory; "
187:            "production_runner performs the exact StaticMemoryPlan and non-static budget gate "
188:            f"({required_bytes} > {available_bytes} bytes)"
189:        )
190:    return capacity

193:def derive_gather_chunk_plan(
194:    frontier_states: int, capacity: int, world_size: int = 2, packet_words: int = 8,
195:) -> GatherChunkPlan:
196:    """Plan fixed-scratch host gather chunks without a capacity-sized packet buffer."""
197:    values = {
198:        "frontier_states": frontier_states,
199:        "capacity": capacity,
200:        "world_size": world_size,
201:        "packet_words": packet_words,
202:    }
203:    if any(isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value <= 0 for value in values.values()):
204:        raise ValueError(f"gather chunk inputs must be positive integers: {values}")
205:    scratch_words = frontier_states * 128 // 8
206:    records_per_chunk = min(
207:        scratch_words // (packet_words * (world_size + 1)), _MAX_GATHER_RECORDS_PER_CHUNK
208:    )
209:    if records_per_chunk <= 0:
210:        raise ValueError("solve bucket gather scratch cannot fit one record per rank")
211:    return GatherChunkPlan(
212:        capacity=capacity,
213:        records_per_chunk=records_per_chunk,
214:        chunk_count=(capacity + records_per_chunk - 1) // records_per_chunk,
215:    )

411:def parse_runner_output(
412:    output: str, result_tsv: Path | None, puzzle_id: int, variant: Variant,
413:) -> ParsedRunnerOutput:
414:    status: CollectionStatus = "not_collected"
415:    if "collection_status=capacity_reached" in output:
416:        status = "capacity_reached"
417:    elif "collection_status=depth_reached" in output:
418:        status = "depth_reached"
419:    records: list[SolutionRecord] = []
420:    if result_tsv is not None and result_tsv.exists():
421:        with result_tsv.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
422:            reader = csv.DictReader(stream, delimiter="\t")
423:            if reader.fieldnames is None or "solution_path" not in reader.fieldnames:
424:                raise ValueError("solve bucket TSV missing solution_path")
425:            for row in reader:
426:                if _parse_uint(row, "puzzle_id") != puzzle_id:
427:                    continue
428:                path = row["solution_path"]
429:                found_depth = _parse_uint(row, "found_depth")
430:                total_depth = _parse_uint(row, "total_depth")
431:                if total_depth < found_depth:
432:                    raise ValueError("solve bucket TSV total_depth is smaller than found_depth")
433:                if _path_depth(path) != total_depth:
434:                    raise ValueError("solve bucket TSV solution_path length does not match total_depth")
435:                records.append(SolutionRecord(
436:                    puzzle_id=puzzle_id,
437:                    variant=variant,
438:                    path=path,
439:                    original_oriented_path=path,
440:                    found_depth=found_depth,
441:                    touch_depth=total_depth - found_depth,
442:                    source_solution_sha256=None,
443:                    valid=True,
444:                    reached_state=(),
445:                ))
446:    if not records:
447:        release_rows: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
448:        for line in _solver_log_lines(output):
449:            if not line.startswith("puzzle_solved=1"):
450:                continue
451:            match = _RELEASE_SOLUTION_RE.fullmatch(line)
452:            legacy = False
453:            if match is None:
454:                match = _RELEASE_SOLUTION_LEGACY_RE.fullmatch(line)
455:                legacy = match is not None
456:            if match is None:
457:                raise ValueError("malformed puzzle_solved=1 release line")
458:            release_puzzle_id = int(match.group("puzzle_id"))
459:            if release_puzzle_id != puzzle_id:
460:                raise ValueError(
461:                    f"release solution puzzle id {release_puzzle_id} does not match requested puzzle id {puzzle_id}"
462:                )
463:            path = match.group("solution")
464:            solution_length = int(match.group("solution_length"))
465:            found_depth = solution_length if legacy else int(match.group("found_depth"))
466:            touch_depth = 0 if legacy else int(match.group("touch_depth"))
467:            if _path_depth(path) != solution_length or found_depth + touch_depth != solution_length:
468:                raise ValueError("release solution length/depth fields do not match solution path")
469:            release_rows.append((path, found_depth, touch_depth))
470:        if release_rows:
471:            for path, found_depth, touch_depth in release_rows:
472:                records.append(SolutionRecord(
473:                    puzzle_id=puzzle_id,
474:                    variant=variant,
475:                    path=path,
476:                    original_oriented_path=path,
477:                    found_depth=found_depth,
478:                    touch_depth=touch_depth,
479:                    source_solution_sha256=None,
480:                    valid=True,
481:                    reached_state=(),
482:                ))
483:        else:
484:            debug_paths = [
485:                match.group("solution")
486:                for line in _solver_log_lines(output)
487:                if (match := _DEBUG_SOLUTION_PATH_RE.fullmatch(line)) is not None
488:            ]
489:            if debug_paths:
490:                path = debug_paths[-1]
491:                records.append(SolutionRecord(
492:                    puzzle_id=puzzle_id,
493:                    variant=variant,
494:                    path=path,
495:                    original_oriented_path=path,
496:                    found_depth=_path_depth(path),
497:                    touch_depth=0,
498:                    source_solution_sha256=None,
499:                    valid=True,
500:                    reached_state=(),
501:                ))
502:        if records and status == "not_collected":
503:            status = "first_solution"
504:    return ParsedRunnerOutput(tuple(records), status)

 State128 apply_solution_moves(
     const State128& initial,
     const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& moves,
     const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& generators) {
     State128 state = initial;
     clear_state_padding(state);
     for (std::uint8_t move : moves) {
         state = apply_move_flat_host(state, generators, move);
     }
     return state;
 }

+struct SolveBucketRecordLess {
+    bool operator()(const SolveBucketRecord& a, const SolveBucketRecord& b) const {
+        if (a.total_depth != b.total_depth) return a.total_depth < b.total_depth;
+        if (a.owner_rank != b.owner_rank) return a.owner_rank < b.owner_rank;
+        if (a.found_depth != b.found_depth) return a.found_depth < b.found_depth;
+        if (a.meta.parent_idx != b.meta.parent_idx) return a.meta.parent_idx < b.meta.parent_idx;
+        if (a.meta.route_packed != b.meta.route_packed) return a.meta.route_packed < b.meta.route_packed;
+        if (a.meta.hash.lo != b.meta.hash.lo) return a.meta.hash.lo < b.meta.hash.lo;
+        if (a.meta.hash.hi != b.meta.hash.hi) return a.meta.hash.hi < b.meta.hash.hi;
+        return a.suffix_id < b.suffix_id;
+    }
+};

 std::uint32_t solved_total_depth(

     ReconstructedSolution& solution,
     const Stream2SuffixRuntime& stream2_suffix,
     std::uint32_t suffix_id,
     const SolvedNeighborhoodRuntime& solved_neighborhood,
     Hash128 hash) {
     if (suffix_id != 0U) {
         append_packed_suffix(solution.moves, stream2_suffix.suffix_for(suffix_id));
     }
     if (!solved_neighborhood.enabled()) {
         return;
     }

     append_packed_suffix(solution.moves, suffix);
 }

 std::uint64_t solve_bucket_gather_records_per_chunk(
     std::uint64_t scratch_words,
     std::uint32_t world_size) {
     constexpr std::uint64_t packet_words = 8ULL;
     if (world_size == 0U) {
         throw std::invalid_argument("solve bucket gather world_size must be positive");
     }
     constexpr std::uint64_t max_host_records_per_chunk = 65'536ULL;
     const std::uint64_t words_per_record_group =
         packet_words * (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(world_size) + 1ULL);
     return std::min<std::uint64_t>(
         scratch_words / words_per_record_group,
         max_host_records_per_chunk);
 }

# Task 5 Report: Existing Runner Orchestration for First and Collect Modes

## Original implementation

Task 5 introduced deterministic two-rank `torch.distributed.run` command construction, first/collect parsing, reflected-search orchestration, `RunArtifacts`, and host-only solve-bucket stop controls. The original reviewed commit was `2f90ed4` (`feat: orchestrate public CayleyPy search modes`).

## Independent review fix round one

The first fix round completed reflection orchestration, real solve-bucket TSV parsing, full local-depth snapshot sizing, hard subprocess/log failures, unique invocation artifacts, live bounded output streaming, manual measured-profile variables, static-hybrid history preflight, guarded scratch cleanup, and synchronized host collection stops. Its standalone commit was `022b5399c8bf81de4bd33693fd927b5137d6ed84`.

## Independent review fix round two

### RED evidence

The second review began from exact commit `022b5399c8bf81de4bd33693fd927b5137d6ed84` and added focused regressions before each implementation slice:

- release first-mode parsing and poisoned inherited environment: `6 failed, 20 passed`;
- external-source records, deterministic reflection-source union, and pre-launch inverse closure: four intended failures;
- solver provenance on an exact external-source duplicate: `2 failed`;
- bounded cursor collection contracts: `4 failed, 31 deselected`;
- live-child stream failure, kill fallback, cleanup masking, and partial artifacts: `4 failed, 35 deselected`;
- rank-symmetric post-reconstruction failure handling: one focused failure;
- rank-local next-K exchange optimization: one focused failure.

### GREEN implementation

First-mode parsing now consumes the real anchored release record, including exact puzzle id, `solution_length`, `found_depth`, `touch_depth`, and an empty solution path. It accepts the legacy release record as `found_depth=solution_length, touch_depth=0`, retains exact-line debug `solution_path` compatibility, and strips only a strict torchrun tee prefix such as `[default0]:`. Unrelated log text is never searched as a substring. Both first-mode C++ release branches emit found/touch depths. Child environments retain ordinary runtime controls such as `PATH` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, but remove every inherited `BEAM_*` and reserved torchrun rank/master/torchelastic variable before applying the explicit invocation contract.

Validated external reflection sources are first-class original-oriented solution candidates before any GPU launch and retain their source SHA-256. Source-only solutions can populate the submission, shorter sources beat longer reflected results, and `after_original` uses a deterministic union of external and newly discovered sources. Exact semantic duplicates retain the stronger original/reflected solver provenance. Generator inverse closure is validated globally before the first original or reflected subprocess.

Collect mode reads only the solved header up front. Each rank scans its device metadata in fixed host chunks of at most 65,536 records, retains only its rank-local next-K after the strict cursor `(total_depth, owner_rank, found_depth, parent_idx, route_packed, hash.lo, hash.hi, suffix_id)`, and exchanges only those bounded next-K packets through fixed NCCL scratch. This is exact because any global next-K record omitted from a rank-local next-K would already have K smaller eligible records on that rank. The global batch remains bounded by the synchronized remaining unique target; the cursor advances on the last raw selected record even when reconstructed paths duplicate, so later scans can fill the requested unique count. Overflow and rank-0 accepted counts are synchronized before depth/pass decisions. Rank-0 validation, path conversion, and output exceptions are captured, collectively propagated after each reconstructed record, and only then rethrown, preventing another rank from entering the next reconstruction collective alone.

After `Popen`, any stream or log-capture exception now stops and reaps torchrun before history deletion, using bounded terminate/wait and kill/wait fallback. Partial combined and available rank diagnostics are retained. The original exception remains primary; teardown or scratch-cleanup failures are attached as notes and never replace it. `run_public_search` exposes a diagnostic `RunArtifacts` snapshot whenever an execution was established.

No CUDA kernel, Stream 1-5 algorithm, device struct, or device-buffer contract was changed.

# Public CayleyPy Task 5 independent-review fix evidence - 2026-07-29

Scope: Python orchestration plus host-only collection control in `production_runner`. CUDA kernels, Stream 1-5 algorithms, device structs, and device-buffer contracts were not changed.

## Round-two TDD evidence

- Release parser/hermetic environment RED: `6 failed, 20 passed`.
- Reflection-source and inverse-closure RED: four intended focused failures.
- Exact source/solver duplicate provenance RED: `2 failed`.
- Bounded cursor collector RED: `4 failed, 31 deselected`.
- Subprocess lifecycle/partial diagnostics RED: `4 failed, 35 deselected`.
- Rank-symmetric processing-error RED: one focused failure.
- Rank-local next-K exchange RED: one focused failure.

## Verified contracts

- anchored release first-mode parsing with strict torchrun-prefix normalization, exact ids/depths/lengths, empty paths, legacy release compatibility, and exact-line debug fallback;
- inherited `BEAM_*` and reserved torchrun rank/master/torchelastic variables removed before the explicit invocation environment, while `PATH` and CUDA visibility remain available;
- validated external sources are original-oriented submission/reflection candidates with SHA provenance; independently discovered exact duplicates retain solver provenance;
- inverse closure and all reflection-source paths fail before any subprocess;
- header-only solved reads plus fixed host metadata chunks, bounded rank-local/global next-K sets, strict cursor order including `found_depth`, and cursor rescans across duplicate reconstructed paths;
- only rank-local next-K packets are NCCL-allgathered, with fixed-scratch exchange chunking and the exactness proof captured in source/tests;
- synchronized header overflow, rank-0 accepted count, batch limit, cursor progression, stop reason, and post-reconstruction rank-0 processing errors;
- bounded terminate/wait then kill/wait fallback before scratch deletion, partial combined/available-rank diagnostics, and cleanup notes that do not mask the primary exception;
- no capacity-sized host candidate vector and no stored vector of all accepted collection records.

    const char* value = std::getenv(name);
    if (value == nullptr || value[0] == '\0') {
        return default_value;
    }
    const std::uint64_t parsed = parse_u64(value, name);
    if (parsed > std::numeric_limits<std::uint32_t>::max()) {
        throw std::invalid_argument(std::string("env value exceeds uint32: ") + name);
    }
    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(parsed);
}

std::uint64_t env_u64(const char* name, std::uint64_t default_value) {
    const char* value = std::getenv(name);
    if (value == nullptr || value[0] == '\0') {
        return default_value;
    }
    return parse_u64(value, name);
}

bool env_present(const char* name) {
    const char* value = std::getenv(name);
    return value != nullptr && value[0] != '\0';

  193: def derive_gather_chunk_plan(
  194:     frontier_states: int, capacity: int, world_size: int = 2, packet_words: int = 8,
  195: ) -> GatherChunkPlan:
  196:     """Plan fixed-scratch host gather chunks without a capacity-sized packet buffer."""
  197:     values = {
  198:         "frontier_states": frontier_states,
  199:         "capacity": capacity,
  200:         "world_size": world_size,
  201:         "packet_words": packet_words,
  202:     }
  203:     if any(isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value <= 0 for value in values.values()):
  204:         raise ValueError(f"gather chunk inputs must be positive integers: {values}")
  205:     scratch_words = frontier_states * 128 // 8
  206:     records_per_chunk = min(
  207:         scratch_words // (packet_words * (world_size + 1)), _MAX_GATHER_RECORDS_PER_CHUNK
  208:     )
  209:     if records_per_chunk <= 0:
  210:         raise ValueError("solve bucket gather scratch cannot fit one record per rank")
  211:     return GatherChunkPlan(
  212:         capacity=capacity,
  213:         records_per_chunk=records_per_chunk,
  214:         chunk_count=(capacity + records_per_chunk - 1) // records_per_chunk,
  215:     )

  305: def _runtime_env(config: PublicRunConfig, plan: RuntimePlan, weights_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
  306:     return {
  307:         "BEAM_WEIGHT_DIR": str(weights_dir),
  308:         "BEAM_PUZZLE_INFO_JSON": str(config.puzzle_info_json),
  309:         "BEAM_GENERATOR_PATH": str(config.puzzle_info_json),
  310:         "BEAM_TEST_CSV": str(config.test_csv),
  311:         "BEAM_RUNTIME_CONFIG_MODE": "manual",
  312:         "BEAM_B_MICRO": str(plan.runtime["b_micro"]),
  313:         "BEAM_STREAM1_CONCURRENCY": str(plan.runtime["stream1_concurrency"]),
  314:         "BEAM_STREAM3_RING_SLOTS": str(plan.runtime["stream3_ring_slots"]),
  315:         "BEAM_SHARD_COUNT": str(plan.runtime["shard_count"]),
  316:         "BEAM_SHARD_BUFFER_COUNT": "2",
  317:         "BEAM_SHARD_CAPACITY_CANDIDATES": str(plan.shard_capacity_candidates),
  318:         "BEAM_STREAM4_BATCH_CANDIDATES": str(plan.runtime["stream4_batch_candidates"]),
  319:         "BEAM_STREAM4_TRIGGER_CANDIDATES": str(plan.runtime["stream4_trigger_candidates"]),
  320:         "BEAM_STREAM4_ACTIVE_SORT_SLOTS": str(plan.runtime["stream4_active_sort_slots"]),
  321:         "BEAM_GLOBAL_SPILL_CAPACITY": "0",
  322:         "BEAM_STREAM5_RECV_CAPACITY_SCALE_PPM": "1000000",
  323:         "BEAM_GPU_HEADROOM_BYTES": str(_T4_HEADROOM_BYTES),
  324:         "BEAM_SOLVED_NEIGHBORHOOD_RADIUS": str(config.touch_bfs_radius),
  325:         "BEAM_REPAIR_K1_RADIUS": str(config.touch_bfs_radius),
  326:         "BEAM_REPAIR_K2_RADIUS": "0",
  327:         "BEAM_STREAM2_SUFFIX_RADIUS": "0",
  328:         "BEAM_DEPTH_LOG_EVERY": "1",
  329:     }
  330: 
  331: 
  332: def build_runner_invocation(
  333:     config: PublicRunConfig,
  334:     plan: RuntimePlan,
  335:     move_count: int,
  336:     puzzle_id: int,
  337:     variant: Variant,
  338:     weights_dir: Path,
  339:     artifact_dir: Path,
  340:     *,
  341:     runner_path: str = "production_runner",
  342:     source_solution_sha256: str | None = None,
  343: ) -> RunnerInvocation:
  344:     """Build a hermetic two-rank torchrun invocation for exactly one variant."""
  345:     run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
  346:     run_root = artifact_dir / f"puzzle-{puzzle_id}" / variant / run_id
  347:     torchrun_log_dir = run_root / "torchrun"
  348:     history_dir = Path(_HISTORY_ROOT.as_posix()) / run_id / str(puzzle_id) / variant
  349:     result_tsv = run_root / "solve_bucket.tsv" if config.solution_mode == "collect" else None
  350:     preflight_history_runtime(config, plan, move_count, history_dir)
  351:     run_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
  352:     env = _runtime_env(config, plan, weights_dir)
  353:     env.update({
  354:         "BEAM_HISTORY_MODE": _HISTORY_MODE,
  355:         "BEAM_HISTORY_SLOT_COUNT": str(_HISTORY_SLOT_COUNT),
  356:         "BEAM_HISTORY_WORKERS": str(_HISTORY_WORKERS),
  357:         "BEAM_HISTORY_RAM_BYTES": str(_HISTORY_RAM_BYTES),
  358:         "BEAM_HISTORY_DISK_BYTES": str(_HISTORY_DISK_BYTES),
  359:         "BEAM_HISTORY_DIR": history_dir.as_posix(),
  360:         "BEAM_HISTORY_DISK_PATH": history_dir.as_posix(),
  361:     })
  362:     env["BEAM_NCCL_ID_FILE"] = str(run_root / "nccl-id.bin")
  363:     if result_tsv is not None:
  364:         snapshot_capacity = derive_solved_result_capacity(plan, move_count)
  365:         derive_gather_chunk_plan(plan.local_beam, snapshot_capacity)
  366:         env.update({
  367:             "BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_MODE": "1",
  368:             "BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_STOP_DEPTH": str(config.collect_until_depth),
  369:             "BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_MAX_SOLUTIONS": str(config.max_collected_solutions),
  370:             "BEAM_SOLVED_RESULT_CAPACITY": str(snapshot_capacity),
  371:             "BEAM_SOLVE_BUCKET_RESULT_TSV": str(result_tsv),
  372:         })
  373:     command = (
  374:         "python", "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node=2",
  375:         "--rdzv-backend=c10d", f"--rdzv-endpoint=127.0.0.1:{_free_port()}", f"--rdzv-id={run_id}",
  376:         f"--log-dir={torchrun_log_dir}", "--redirects=3", "--tee=0:3", "--no-python", runner_path,
  377:         str(puzzle_id), str(config.max_depth), str(config.beam_width),
  378:     )
  379:     return RunnerInvocation(
  380:         command=command,
  381:         env=env,
  382:         result_tsv=result_tsv,
  383:         combined_log=run_root / "combined.log",
  384:         rank_logs=(run_root / "rank-0.log", run_root / "rank-1.log"),
  385:         torchrun_log_dir=torchrun_log_dir,
  386:         history_dir=history_dir,
  387:         puzzle_id=puzzle_id,
  388:         variant=variant,
  389:         source_solution_sha256=source_solution_sha256,
  390:     )

---
name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence в‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter в‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion в‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
вњ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
вќЊ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
вњ… Write в†’ Run (pass) в†’ Revert fix в†’ Run (MUST FAIL) в†’ Restore в†’ Run (pass)
вќЊ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
вњ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
вќЊ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
вњ… Re-read plan в†’ Create checklist в†’ Verify each в†’ Report gaps or completion
вќЊ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
вњ… Agent reports success в†’ Check VCS diff в†’ Verify changes в†’ Report actual state
вќЊ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
# Project Agent Rules

## Operating Rule
- Read `AGENTS.md` before project edits.
- Update `memory/CHANGELOG.md` after meaningful code, config, or architecture changes.
- Update `memory/PROMPTS.md` with user prompts that define requirements.
- Store test outputs, logs, and verification notes under `test_results/`.
- Prefer agent-centered code: explicit contracts, deterministic tests, small files, low hidden state.

## Architecture Source
- Primary architecture contract: `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md`.
- Current Stream 4 implementation rule: use threshold + compact + CUB/fixed-temp sort/reduce + compact; do not use Stream 4 hash-table dedup.

## Implementation Guardrails
- `State128` logical bytes are `v[0..119]`.
- `State128` padding bytes are `v[120..127]`.
- Persistent frontier padding must be zero.
- `FinalResponse` may temporarily store `target_local_idx` in `v[120..123]`.
- `Hash128` is one logical 128-bit key stored as `{lo, hi}`.
- `CandidateMeta` must remain 32 bytes and 32-byte aligned.
- Stream 3 payload id must be original candidate id, not compact index.
- Stream 4 must not apply shard top-k or semantic shard cap.

 ### GREEN implementation
 
-First-mode parsing now consumes the real anchored release record, including exact puzzle id, `solution_length`, `found_depth`, `touch_depth`, and an empty solution path. It accepts the legacy release record as `found_depth=solution_length, touch_depth=0`, retains exact-line debug `solution_path` compatibility, and strips only a strict torchrun tee prefix such as `[default0]:`. Unrelated log text is never searched as a substring. Both first-mode C++ release branches emit found/touch depths. +First-mode parsing now consumes the real anchored release record, including exact puzzle id, `solution_length`, `found_depth`, `touch_depth`, and an empty solution path. It accepts the legacy release record as `found_depth=solution_length, touch_depth=0`, retains exact-line debug `solution_path` compatibility, and normalizes exactly the fixed `--tee=0:3` rank-0 prefix `[default0]:`; hostile lookalike prefixes remain ordinary unrelated text. Release seconds use a nonnegative decimal grammar with an optional valid exponent and must convert to a finite float. Unrelated log text is never searched as a substring. Both first-mode C++ release branches emit found/touch depths. Child environments retain ordinary runtime controls such as `PATH` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, but remove every inherited `BEAM_*` and reserved torchrun rank/master/torchelastic variable before applying the explicit invocation contract.
 
 Validated external reflection sources are first-class original-oriented solution candidates before any GPU launch and retain their source SHA-256. Source-only solutions can populate the submission, shorter sources beat longer reflected results, and `after_original` uses a deterministic union of external and newly discovered sources. Exact semantic duplicates retain the stronger original/reflected solver provenance. Generator inverse closure is validated globally before the first original or reflected subprocess.
 
 Collect mode reads only the solved header up front. Each rank scans its device metadata in fixed host chunks of at most 65,536 records, retains only its rank-local next-K after the strict cursor `(total_depth, owner_rank, found_depth, parent_idx, route_packed, hash.lo, hash.hi, suffix_id)`, and exchanges only those bounded next-K packets through fixed NCCL scratch. This is exact because any global next-K record omitted from a rank-local next-K would already have K smaller eligible records on that rank. The global batch remains bounded by the synchronized remaining unique target; the cursor advances on the last raw selected record even when reconstructed paths duplicate, so later scans can fill the requested unique count. Overflow and rank-0 accepted counts are synchronized before depth/pass decisions. Rank-0 validation, path conversion, and output exceptions are captured, collectively propagated after each reconstructed record, and only then rethrown, preventing another rank from entering the next reconstruction collective alone.
 
 After `Popen`, any stream or log-capture exception now stops and reaps torchrun before history deletion, using bounded terminate/wait and kill/wait fallback. Partial combined and available rank diagnostics are retained. The original exception remains primary; teardown or scratch-cleanup failures are attached as notes and never replace it. `run_public_search` exposes a diagnostic `RunArtifacts` snapshot whenever an execution was established.
 
 No CUDA kernel, Stream 1-5 algorithm, device struct, or device-buffer contract was changed.

# Work With Kaggle

Use this skill whenever the task involves Kaggle notebooks, kernels, datasets, or GPU validation runs.

## Project Memory First

For project repositories, read local project guidance before changing notebooks or source:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `memory/PROMPTS.md` and `memory/CHANGELOG.md`, especially recent Kaggle entries
- relevant `test_results/kaggle_*` reports for the same failure/config family

This project has many Kaggle-specific decisions preserved in memory. Do not assume a generic Kaggle workflow is correct when project memory says otherwise.

## Safety And Scope

- Do not upload or publish current uncommitted source to a Kaggle dataset unless the user explicitly approves external export.
- Prefer GitHub-backed Kaggle source when the user has selected GitHub as source of truth.
- Do not push a public Kaggle notebook/kernel unless the user explicitly approves publication or public push.
- Do not make C++/CUDA algorithmic changes while diagnosing Kaggle failures unless the user explicitly approves code changes. Config-only notebook changes are acceptable when useful and consistent with the request.
- Do not revert unrelated local changes. Kaggle notebook edits often coexist with dirty source changes.
- For multi-rank validation, do not fake `WORLD_SIZE=2` on one GPU with both ranks on `LOCAL_RANK=0` unless the user explicitly approves that limited smoke. Real multi-rank validation should use real multi-GPU hardware such as Kaggle 2xT4.

## Kaggle CLI Workflow

Prefer Kaggle CLI for authenticated Kaggle work:

- Check metadata before pushing: `kaggle/kernel-metadata.json` or the selected push package metadata.
- Validate notebooks locally before push: JSON parse and Python AST parse for code cells.
- Push with the intended package directory, then monitor with `kaggle kernels status <owner/slug>`.
- Download outputs/logs after completion or failure and store them under `test_results/`.
- If CLI network/proxy behavior is project-specific, inspect existing scripts/config and preserve local proxy-bypass behavior instead of switching tools silently.

When reporting command output to the user, summarize the important status/version/error lines. The user does not see raw command output.

## Notebook Preparation Rules

For solver notebooks in this project:

- Keep a first config cell with the main run parameters such as beam, depth, puzzle range, model weights URL/path, history mode, and torchrun topology.
- Keep build/checkouts and large transient trees under `/tmp` where possible. Use `/kaggle/working` for logs, CSVs, summaries, and final artifacts.
- Add a preflight cell for large runs: compute local/global beam, world size, shard capacity, Stream1/3/4 guards, static history RAM/disk budgets, and free disk under `/tmp` before clone/build/run.
- Clean stale `/tmp/beam_history_*` and configured history disk paths before runs and between puzzles when static-hybrid history is used.
- For long multi-rank runs, stream selected rank logs live while writing full rank logs to disk.
- Final cells should summarize results and produce user-useful CSV/PNG artifacts, for example solved counts and solution-length histograms.

## Torchrun And Multi-GPU Rules

- Torchrun notebooks should launch the existing binary/processes through explicit topology settings, not implicit GPU auto-detection.
- Expose `TORCHRUN_NPROC_PER_NODE`, `TORCHRUN_NNODES`, `TORCHRUN_NODE_RANK`, and rendezvous endpoint/port in config.
- Derive `WORLD_SIZE` from torchrun topology settings, not from `torch.cuda.device_count()` alone.
- For C++ multi-rank runs, torchrun or Python launchers should only start processes. C++ reads `RANK`, `LOCAL_RANK`, and `WORLD_SIZE`, calls `cudaSetDevice(LOCAL_RANK)`, and creates NCCL communicators itself.
- H100 and T4 notebooks may differ by CUDA architecture/build directory and hardware-specific config, but should otherwise stay comparable when the user asks for paired notebooks.

## Monitoring And Stop Rules

- For diagnostic Kaggle runs, if the user has asked Codex to watch logs and no new logs appear for about 120 seconds, stop the run and inspect downloaded logs. This rule came from project memory and applies to diagnostic/watch tasks.
- Do not stop production/no-timeout runs unless the user explicitly asks or the notebook itself has a configured timeout.
- If a run appears hung because stdout is redirected, check rank log files and whether live-rank streaming is enabled before assuming a stall.
- Preserve logs even when stopping: terminate gracefully when possible, then download output files.

## Failure Diagnosis Checklist

After a Kaggle failure, collect and scan:

- Kaggle worker status and kernel version
- notebook stdout tail
- rank logs under the notebook output directory
- result JSONL/CSV summaries
- GPU budget/preflight output
- explicit Kaggle messages such as disk quota failures

Common patterns in this project:

- `KernelWorkerStatus.ERROR` plus "more disk space than is available" usually means disk quota/static history arena pressure.
- `return_code=-9` can indicate host RAM OOM.
- `code=3002` / `STREAM_FATAL_STREAM3_DOUBLE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW` points to Stream3/Stream4/threshold/capacity flow diagnostics.
- `final selected count does not match score phase counts` points to final selection/histogram/exact-count mismatch.
- `cudaGraphInstantiate: out of memory` may require config-only headroom/shard-capacity changes before deeper code work.
- Silent output after build may simply mean rank stdout is redirected and live rank logging is disabled.

Write a short report under `test_results/` for meaningful Kaggle validations, sweeps, failures, or launches.

## Response Style

- Be explicit about whether you changed source code, notebook config only, or only launched/monitored a run.
- Include Kaggle kernel slug/version/status when known.
- Include exact local report/log paths in `test_results/`.
- Keep recommendations tied to evidence from logs, not guesses.
- If the next step requires exporting source or publishing publicly, ask for explicit approval first.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence в‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter в‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion в‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
вњ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
вќЊ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
вњ… Write в†’ Run (pass) в†’ Revert fix в†’ Run (MUST FAIL) в†’ Restore в†’ Run (pass)
вќЊ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
вњ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
вќЊ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
вњ… Re-read plan в†’ Create checklist в†’ Verify each в†’ Report gaps or completion
вќЊ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
вњ… Agent reports success в†’ Check VCS diff в†’ Verify changes в†’ Report actual state
вќЊ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
# Project Agent Rules

## Operating Rule
- Read `AGENTS.md` before project edits.
- Update `memory/CHANGELOG.md` after meaningful code, config, or architecture changes.
- Update `memory/PROMPTS.md` with user prompts that define requirements.
- Store test outputs, logs, and verification notes under `test_results/`.
- Prefer agent-centered code: explicit contracts, deterministic tests, small files, low hidden state.

## Architecture Source
- Primary architecture contract: `ARCHITECTURE_NEED.md`.
- Current Stream 4 implementation rule: use threshold + compact + CUB/fixed-temp sort/reduce + compact; do not use Stream 4 hash-table dedup.

## Implementation Guardrails
- `State128` logical bytes are `v[0..119]`.
- `State128` padding bytes are `v[120..127]`.
- Persistent frontier padding must be zero.
- `FinalResponse` may temporarily store `target_local_idx` in `v[120..123]`.
- `Hash128` is one logical 128-bit key stored as `{lo, hi}`.
- `CandidateMeta` must remain 32 bytes and 32-byte aligned.
- Stream 3 payload id must be original candidate id, not compact index.
- Stream 4 must not apply shard top-k or semantic shard cap.

# Task 5 Report: Existing Runner Orchestration for First and Collect Modes

## Original implementation

Task 5 introduced deterministic two-rank `torch.distributed.run` command construction, first/collect parsing, reflected-search orchestration, `RunArtifacts`, and host-only solve-bucket stop controls. The original reviewed commit was `2f90ed4` (`feat: orchestrate public CayleyPy search modes`).

## Independent review fix round one

The first fix round completed reflection orchestration, real solve-bucket TSV parsing, full local-depth snapshot sizing, hard subprocess/log failures, unique invocation artifacts, live bounded output streaming, manual measured-profile variables, static-hybrid history preflight, guarded scratch cleanup, and synchronized host collection stops. Its standalone commit was `022b5399c8bf81de4bd33693fd927b5137d6ed84`.

## Independent review fix round two

### RED evidence

The second review began from exact commit `022b5399c8bf81de4bd33693fd927b5137d6ed84` and added focused regressions before each implementation slice:

- release first-mode parsing and poisoned inherited environment: `6 failed, 20 passed`;
- external-source records, deterministic reflection-source union, and pre-launch inverse closure: four intended failures;
- solver provenance on an exact external-source duplicate: `2 failed`;
- bounded cursor collection contracts: `4 failed, 31 deselected`;
- live-child stream failure, kill fallback, cleanup masking, and partial artifacts: `4 failed, 35 deselected`;
- rank-symmetric post-reconstruction failure handling: one focused failure;
- rank-local next-K exchange optimization: one focused failure.
- exact-prefix and finite-seconds parser P2: `6 failed, 2 passed, 41 deselected` before the narrow fix.

### GREEN implementation

First-mode parsing now consumes the real anchored release record, including exact puzzle id, `solution_length`, `found_depth`, `touch_depth`, and an empty solution path. It accepts the legacy release record as `found_depth=solution_length, touch_depth=0`, retains exact-line debug `solution_path` compatibility, and normalizes exactly the fixed `--tee=0:3` rank-0 prefix `[default0]:`; hostile lookalike prefixes remain ordinary unrelated text. Release seconds use a nonnegative decimal grammar with an optional valid exponent and must convert to a finite float. Unrelated log text is never searched as a substring. Both first-mode C++ release branches emit found/touch depths. Child environments retain ordinary runtime controls such as `PATH` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, but remove every inherited `BEAM_*` and reserved torchrun rank/master/torchelastic variable before applying the explicit invocation contract.

Validated external reflection sources are first-class original-oriented solution candidates before any GPU launch and retain their source SHA-256. Source-only solutions can populate the submission, shorter sources beat longer reflected results, and `after_original` uses a deterministic union of external and newly discovered sources. Exact semantic duplicates retain the stronger original/reflected solver provenance. Generator inverse closure is validated globally before the first original or reflected subprocess.

Collect mode reads only the solved header up front. Each rank scans its device metadata in fixed host chunks of at most 65,536 records, retains only its rank-local next-K after the strict cursor `(total_depth, owner_rank, found_depth, parent_idx, route_packed, hash.lo, hash.hi, suffix_id)`, and exchanges only those bounded next-K packets through fixed NCCL scratch. This is exact because any global next-K record omitted from a rank-local next-K would already have K smaller eligible records on that rank. The global batch remains bounded by the synchronized remaining unique target; the cursor advances on the last raw selected record even when reconstructed paths duplicate, so later scans can fill the requested unique count. Overflow and rank-0 accepted counts are synchronized before depth/pass decisions. Rank-0 validation, path conversion, and output exceptions are captured, collectively propagated after each reconstructed record, and only then rethrown, preventing another rank from entering the next reconstruction collective alone.

After `Popen`, any stream or log-capture exception now stops and reaps torchrun before history deletion, using bounded terminate/wait and kill/wait fallback. Partial combined and available rank diagnostics are retained. The original exception remains primary; teardown or scratch-cleanup failures are attached as notes and never replace it. `run_public_search` exposes a diagnostic `RunArtifacts` snapshot whenever an execution was established.

No CUDA kernel, Stream 1-5 algorithm, device struct, or device-buffer contract was changed.

  68: def _write_run(root: Path, name: str, combined: str, *, tsv: bytes | None = None) -> dict[str, object]:
  69:     run_dir = root / "runs" / name
  70:     run_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
  71:     combined_path = run_dir / "combined.log"
  72:     combined_path.write_text(combined, encoding="utf-8")
  73:     for rank in (0, 1):
  74:         (run_dir / f"rank{rank}.stdout.log").write_text(
  75:             f"rank={rank} normal_completion=1\n", encoding="utf-8"
  76:         )
  77:         (run_dir / f"rank{rank}.stderr.log").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
  78:     if tsv is not None:
  79:         (run_dir / "solutions.tsv").write_bytes(tsv)
  80:     gpu_rows = ["0, Tesla T4, 1, 15359, 15360", "1, Tesla T4, 1, 15359, 15360"]
  81:     result = {
  82:         "name": name,
  83:         "mode": "first" if name == "first" else "collect",
  84:         "command": [
  85:             "python", "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node=2",
  86:             "--redirects=3", "--tee=0:3", "production_runner",
  87:             str(PUZZLE_ID), str(DEPTH_LIMIT), str(BEAM_WIDTH),
  88:         ],
  89:         "return_code": 0,
  90:         "rank_return_codes": {"0": 0, "1": 0},
  91:         "rank_return_code_basis": "torchrun rc=0 requires every local worker to exit zero",
  92:         "timed_out": False,
  93:         "elapsed_sec": 1.25,
  94:         "peak_process_tree_rss_bytes": 123456,
  95:         "rss_sample_count": 1,
  96:         "rss_samples_retained": 1,
  97:         "rss_samples": [{"elapsed_sec": 0.1, "rss_bytes": 123456, "process_count": 3}],
  98:         "combined_log_bytes": len(combined_path.read_bytes()),
  99:         "combined_log_sha256": sha256(combined_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
 100:         "rank_stdout_count": 2,
 101:         "rank_stderr_count": 2,
 102:         "gpu_before": gpu_rows,
 103:         "gpu_after": gpu_rows,
 104:         "fatal_hits": [],
 105:         "normal_completion_both_ranks": True,
 106:     }
 107:     (run_dir / "run_result.json").write_text(json.dumps(result) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
 108:     return result

 111: def _write_fake_gate(
 112:     root: Path,
 113:     *,
 114:     mismatch: bool = False,
 115:     first_solution: str = "BR",
 116: ) -> None:
 117:     source_sha = sha256(REVIEWED_SOURCE.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
 118:     binary_sha = "b" * 64
 119:     manifest = {
 120:         "kernel_slug": KERNEL_SLUG,
 121:         "base_git_rev": BASE_GIT_REV,
 122:         "reviewed_commit": REVIEWED_COMMIT,
 123:         "base_production_runner_sha256": "a" * 64,
 124:         "production_runner_sha256": source_sha,
 125:         "production_runner_bytes": REVIEWED_SOURCE.stat().st_size,
 126:         "binary_sha256": binary_sha,
 127:         "binary_bytes": 1234567,
 128:         "cutlass_git_rev": CUTLASS_GIT_REV,
 129:         "build_type": "Release",
 130:         "cuda_architectures": "75",
 131:         "nccl_linked": True,
 132:         "timings_sec": {
 133:             "base_clone": 1.0,
 134:             "cutlass_clone": 1.0,
 135:             "configure": 1.0,
 136:             "compile": 1.0,
 137:         },
 138:     }
 139:     (root / "source_manifest.json").write_text(
 140:         json.dumps(manifest) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
 141:     )
 142:     gpu_rows = ["0, Tesla T4, 15360, 15359", "1, Tesla T4, 15360, 15359"]
 143:     (root / "environment.json").write_text(
 144:         json.dumps({"gpu_rows": gpu_rows}) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
 145:     )
 146:     (root / "weights_manifest.json").write_text(
 147:         json.dumps({
 148:             "model": {
 149:                 "state_len": 120,
 150:                 "num_classes": 120,
 151:                 "output_dim": 24,
 152:                 "dtype": "fp16",
 153:             },
 154:             "files": {},
 155:         }) + "\n",
 156:         encoding="utf-8",
 157:     )
 158:     (root / "build.log").write_text(
 159:         "cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBEAM_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75\n"
 160:         "ldd production_runner => libnccl.so\n",
 161:         encoding="utf-8",
 162:     )
 163:     (root / "CMakeCache.txt").write_text(
 164:         "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=Release\n", encoding="utf-8"
 165:     )
 166:     first_line = (
 167:         "[default0]:puzzle_solved=1 puzzle_id=1 seconds=0.5 solution_length=1 "
 168:         f"found_depth=1 touch_depth=0 solution={first_solution}\n"
 169:     )
 170:     first = _write_run(root, "first", first_line)
 171:     header = (
 172:         b"puzzle_id\tdepth_index\tfound_depth\ttotal_depth\tknown_length\t"
 173:         b"delta\towner_rank\tsolution_path\n"
 174:     )
 175:     row = b"1\t0\t1\t1\t1\t0\t0\tBR\n"
 176:     collect_bytes = header + row
 177:     collect_a = _write_run(
 178:         root,
 179:         "collect_a",
 180:         "[default0]:collection_status=depth_reached\n",
 181:         tsv=collect_bytes,
 182:     )
 183:     collect_b = _write_run(
 184:         root,
 185:         "collect_b",
 186:         "[default0]:collection_status=depth_reached\n",
 187:         tsv=collect_bytes + (b"1\t1\t2\t2\t1\t1\t1\tBR.BR\n" if mismatch else b""),
 188:     )
 189:     summary = {
 190:         "status": "ok",
 191:         "kernel_slug": KERNEL_SLUG,
 192:         "base_git_rev": BASE_GIT_REV,
 193:         "reviewed_commit": REVIEWED_COMMIT,
 194:         "source_sha256": source_sha,
 195:         "binary_sha256": binary_sha,
 196:         "cutlass_git_rev": CUTLASS_GIT_REV,
 197:         "hardware": gpu_rows,
 198:         "build": manifest,
 199:         "parameters": {
 200:             "puzzle_id": PUZZLE_ID,
 201:             "beam_width": BEAM_WIDTH,
 202:             "depth_limit": DEPTH_LIMIT,
 203:             "max_unique_solutions": MAX_UNIQUE_SOLUTIONS,
 204:             "solved_result_capacity": SOLVED_RESULT_CAPACITY,
 205:             "k1_radius": K1_RADIUS,
 206:             "k2_radius": K2_RADIUS,
 207:             "profile": MEASURED_PROFILE,
 208:         },
 209:         "first_release_line": first_line.strip(),
 210:         "first_release": {
 211:             "seconds": 0.5,
 212:             "solution_length": 1,
 213:             "found_depth": 1,
 214:             "touch_depth": 0,
 215:             "solution": first_solution,
 216:         },
 217:         "cpu_solution_valid": True,
 218:         "collection_status": {"collect_a": "depth_reached", "collect_b": "depth_reached"},
 219:         "collect_tsv_schema": [

 221:             "known_length", "delta", "owner_rank", "solution_path",
 222:         ],
 223:         "collect_tsv_rows": 1,
 224:         "collect_tsv_unique_paths": 1,

 226:         "collect_tsv_sha256": sha256(collect_bytes).hexdigest(),
 227:         "collect_tsv_byte_identical": True,
 228:         "runs": {"first": first, "collect_a": collect_a, "collect_b": collect_b},
 229:         "no_overflow_oom_timeout_or_collective_hang": True,
 230:         "injected_rank0_failure": "source-test-only-no-safe-runtime-hook",
 231:     }
 232:     (root / "gate_summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

 - Added automatic public Stream1 MLP checkpoint schema detection and fp16 export wrapper. The exporter now supports `--format auto`, accepts only unambiguous BatchNorm-folded or ResMLP-LayerNorm tensor signatures, writes only the checkpoint basename into public manifests, and returns a SHA-256-attested sanitized export contract.
 - Clarified the public model-export contract: callers must provide the selected puzzle state length and move count, so the sanitized export manifest is checked against actual puzzle dimensions and only permits scalar or exact move-count heads.
 - Hardened public automatic Stream1 export: auto CLI now requires fp16 plus explicit puzzle dimensions, validates atomically through a temporary sibling directory, rejects pre-existing output paths, and converts missing schema-matched tensors into a clear public ValueError. Explicit legacy exporter modes retain bf16 support.
 - Made public checkpoint export attestation pre-promotion: the source SHA-256 is computed before exporting and reused after validation, while missing nested output parents are created before temporary sibling allocation.
 
 - Added public CayleyPy 2xT4 runtime-plan derivation from measured profiles. The preflight preserves the requested beam except for documented distributed alignment, derives parent and Stream3 batches from the actual move count, enforces 1024-aligned shard capacity floors, records measured evidence/history budgets, and fails closed for unmeasured profiles or insufficient /tmp history disk. CUDA/C++ algorithms are unchanged.
 
 - Hardened the public CayleyPy 2xT4 runtime plan: only world size 2 is accepted, and the derived runtime mapping is immutable while preflight serialization emits a detached JSON-safe copy.
 
 - Added public CayleyPy Task 4 path helpers: strict dot-separated replay, permutation-derived inverse lookup without name conventions, reflected-state construction, CPU original-path validation, and deterministic semantic solution deduplication.
 - Hardened public CayleyPy Task 4 records and validation: `SolutionRecord` now owns an immutable tuple copy of `reached_state`, and original-solution validation returns `False` for malformed direct generator values while preserving unrelated runtime failures.
 - Added Task 5 public 2xT4 runner orchestration contracts, deterministic torchrun invocation/log capture, bounded collection parsing, and host-only solve-bucket depth/capacity stops without CUDA stream changes.
 
 ## 2026-07-29
 - Hardened public CayleyPy Task 5 orchestration after independent review: complete reflection modes and CPU revalidation, real solve-bucket TSV parsing, semantic result deduplication, hard subprocess/log failures, retained per-invocation artifacts, live rank-0 streaming, exact manual 2xT4 runtime variables, bounded static-hybrid history preflight, and guarded scratch cleanup.
 - Reworked Task 5 collect-mode host controls without changing CUDA kernels or Stream 1-5 algorithms: the solved snapshot now covers the full local one-depth Stream2 bound, distributed records gather in bounded chunks through existing scratch, and overflow/capacity/depth stop reasons synchronize across ranks with explicit depth taking precedence over the legacy window.
 - Completed Task 5 review round two: first-mode parsing now accepts anchored release output with exact found/touch depths and strict torchrun-prefix normalization; the child environment removes inherited solver/torchrun controls; validated external paths are source candidates before launch; inverse closure is globally prevalidated; and exact source/solver duplicates retain discovered provenance.
 - Replaced capacity-sized collect-mode host snapshots with header-only reads, fixed 65,536-record metadata scans, strict cursor batches, and exact rank-local next-K exchange through fixed NCCL scratch. Accepted counts, overflow, cursor progress, and rank-0 post-reconstruction errors are synchronized across ranks; duplicate paths trigger later cursor passes until the unique target is filled.
 - Made public runner teardown exception-safe: stream/log failures terminate and reap torchrun with bounded kill fallback before scratch cleanup, retain partial diagnostics, and attach cleanup failures without masking the primary exception.
 - Hardened Task 5 release-log parsing after the P2 review: only the fixed `--tee=0:3` prefix `[default0]:` is normalized, hostile lookalike prefixes are ignored, and seconds must use a nonnegative decimal grammar with an optional valid exponent and convert to a finite float.
+- Added the private Task 5 real-2xT4 Kaggle acceptance package and independent downloaded-evidence validator. The package clones exact public base SHA `6f95bd6`, overlays the full SHA-attested reviewed `production_runner.cu`, builds Release SM75 with CUTLASS/NCCL, and captures full build, GPU, process-tree RSS, per-rank, first-mode, and repeated collect-mode evidence without changing C++/CUDA algorithms. Narrow binary attributes preserve byte-exact upstream CMake/combined/kernel logs without normalizing their formatting.
+- Completed private Kaggle kernel `trydotatwo/cayleypy-public-task-5-2xt4-gate` v2. Exactly two T4s returned a CPU-valid `BR` first solution and two normal 16-path collections with byte-identical TSV SHA-256 `74c12063c3f7cd6399546d6dd865d537e966bf8d9b935510174f9d46a92c748e`; downloaded raw evidence and the compact report are under `test_results/`.

IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?\n2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)\n3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures\n4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?\n   - If NO: State actual status with evidence\n   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence\n5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim\n\nSkip any step = lying, not verifying\n```\n\n## Common Failures\n\n| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |\n|-------|----------|----------------|\n| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, \"should pass\" |\n| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |\n| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |\n| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |\n| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |\n| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports \"success\" |\n| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |\n\n## Red Flags - STOP\n\n- Using \"should\", \"probably\", \"seems to\"\n- Expressing satisfaction before verification (\"Great!\", \"Perfect!\", \"Done!\", etc.)\n- About to commit/push/PR without verification\n- Trusting agent success reports\n- Relying on partial verification\n- Thinking \"just this once\"\n- Tired and wanting work over\n- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**\n\n## Rationalization Prevention\n\n| Excuse | Reality |\n|--------|---------|\n| \"Should work now\" | RUN the verification |\n| \"I'm confident\" | Confidence в‰  evidence |\n| \"Just this once\" | No exceptions |\n| \"Linter passed\" | Linter в‰  compiler |\n| \"Agent said success\" | Verify independently |\n| \"I'm tired\" | Exhaustion в‰  excuse |\n| \"Partial check is enough\" | Partial proves nothing |\n| \"Different words so rule doesn't apply\" | Spirit over letter |\n\n## Key Patterns\n\n**Tests:**\n```\nвњ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] \"All tests pass\"\nвќЊ \"Should pass now\" / \"Looks correct\"\n```\n\n**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**\n```\nвњ… Write в†’ Run (pass) в†’ Revert fix в†’ Run (MUST FAIL) в†’ Restore в†’ Run (pass)\nвќЊ \"I've written a regression test\" (without red-green verification)\n```\n\n**Build:**\n```\nвњ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] \"Build passes\"\nвќЊ \"Linter passed\" (linter doesn't check compilation)\n```\n\n**Requirements:**\n```\nвњ… Re-read plan в†’ Create checklist в†’ Verify each в†’ Report gaps or completion\nвќЊ \"Tests pass, phase complete\"\n```\n\n**Agent delegation:**\n```\nвњ… Agent reports success в†’ Check VCS diff в†’ Verify changes Use `/kaggle/working` for logs, CSVs, summaries, and final artifacts.\n- Add a preflight cell for large runs: compute local/global beam, world size, shard capacity, Stream1/3/4 guards, static history RAM/disk budgets, and free disk under `/tmp` before clone/build/run.\n- Clean stale `/tmp/beam_history_*` and configured history disk paths before runs and between puzzles when static-hybrid history is used.\n- For long multi-rank runs, stream selected rank logs live while writing full rank logs to disk.\n- Final cells should summarize results and produce user-useful CSV/PNG artifacts, for example solved counts and solution-length histograms.\n\n## Torchrun And Multi-GPU Rules\n\n- Torchrun notebooks should launch the existing binary/processes through explicit topology settings, not implicit GPU auto-detection.\n- Expose `TORCHRUN_NPROC_PER_NODE`, `TORCHRUN_NNODES`, `TORCHRUN_NODE_RANK`, and rendezvous endpoint/port in config.\n- Derive `WORLD_SIZE` from torchrun topology settings, not from `torch.cuda.device_count()` alone.\n- For C++ multi-rank runs, torchrun or Python launchers should only start processes. This rule came from project memory and applies to diagnostic/watch tasks.\n- Do not stop production/no-timeout runs unless the user explicitly asks or the notebook itself has a configured timeout.\n- If a run appears hung because stdout is redirected, check rank log files and whether live-rank streaming is enabled before assuming a stall.\n- Preserve logs even when stopping: terminate gracefully when possible, then download output files.\n\n## Failure Diagnosis Checklist\n\nAfter a Kaggle failure, collect and scan:\n\n- Kaggle worker status and kernel version\n- notebook stdout tail\n- rank logs under the notebook output directory\n- result JSONL/CSV summaries\n- GPU budget/preflight output\n- explicit Kaggle messages such as disk quota failures\n\nCommon patterns in this project:\n\n- `KernelWorkerStatus.ERROR` plus \"more disk space than is available\" usually means disk quota/static history arena pressure.\n- `return_code=-9` can indicate host RAM OOM.\n- `code=3002` / `STREAM_FATAL_STREAM3_DOUBLE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW` points to Stream3/Stream4/threshold/capacity flow diagnostics.\n- `final selected count does not match score phase counts` points to final selection/histogram/exact-count mismatch.\n- `cudaGraphInstantiate: out of memory` may require config-only headroom/shard-capacity changes before deeper code work.\n- Silent output after build may simply mean rank stdout is redirected and live rank logging is disabled.\n\nWrite a short report under `test_results/` for meaningful Kaggle validations, sweeps, failures, or launches.\n\n## Response Style\n\n- Be explicit about whether you changed source code, notebook config only, or only launched/monitored a run.\n- Include Kaggle kernel slug/version/status when known.\n- Include exact local report/log paths in `test_results/`.\n- Keep recommendations tied to evidence from logs, not guesses.\n- If the next step requires exporting source or publishing publicly, ask for explicit approval first.\r\n"}

This prevents an assumed config value from reclassifying a native App session as bridge-owned.\n\nStatic native V2 accepts both `[features] multi_agent_v2 = true` and `[features.multi_agent_v2] enabled = true`.
